question: According to DSM-5 / ICD-11 criteria, what is the MINIMUM duration of symptoms required to diagnose a Major Depressive Episode (MDE)?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: One week is the minimum duration for a manic episode, not a depressive episode.
Correct. A MDE requires depressed mood and/or anhedonia plus associated neurovegetative symptoms persisting for at least 2 weeks.
One month is not the threshold — 2 weeks is required. Longer duration increases certainty but the minimum is 2 weeks.
Six months is the persistence criterion for dysthymia (persistent depressive disorder), not a single MDE.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the DSM-5 MDE criteria. The minimum duration is 2 weeks — different from mania (≥1 week) and dysthymia (≥6 months).
Well done. The 2-week minimum is the critical gate for diagnosing MDE — distinguishing pathological depression from normal grief or transient low mood.
